name: Vitalios of Alexandria
life: The Monk Vitalios (†VII century) undertook a hidden and extraordinary ascetic exploit in Alexandria during the patriarchate of St. John the Merciful. He compiled a list of all the fallen women of the city and visited each in turn, paying for their virtue for one night while he spent the night in prayer on their behalf. Many repented and entered monasteries or respectable life. He endured public mockery and slander without defense, leaving at his death a scroll reading: 'Men of Alexandria, judge not beforehand, till cometh the Lord, the Righteous Judge.'
